l1: What is the source build and the target build of the upgrade?
What is the exact 0xC1900101 (or other) rollback error code shown?
Which of the four upgrade phases failed — Downlevel, SafeOS, First boot, or Second boot?
Did the upgrade fail during download, install, or first boot?
Is this upgrade part of a broader ring-based rollout (pilot/broad/critical rings), or a one-off manual upgrade?
l2: Is there a known incompatible driver, filter driver, or application blocking the upgrade?
Is the device using BitLocker, and was it suspended prior to upgrade?
Is Citrix VDA, non-Microsoft disk encryption, or antivirus software installed on this device?
Were user profile folders redirected off the OS drive (e.g. to E:)?
Does setupact.log show a device install that has been running for more than 5 minutes without closing (an unclosed '<ins>' log section)?

l1: Run 'winver' to confirm the current build before and after attempts.
Check $Windows.~BT\Sources\Panther\setupact.log for down-level phase failures — this is the primary log for diagnosing setup issues.
Check setuperr.log (same folder) for all errors encountered during installation.
Check available free disk space — 16GB for 32-bit, 20GB for 64-bit.
Search Windows 10 setupact.log for 'Operations recap' to quickly jump to the phase and last operation that was executed, and whether it succeeded.
l2: Run SetupDiag.exe against the failed upgrade attempt to get a documented rollback profile match and diagnosis code.
For OOBE-phase failures (0x4001C–0x4001F), check $Windows.~BT\Sources\Panther\UnattendGC\setupact.log.
For generic rollbacks (0xC1900101), check $Windows.~BT\Sources\Rollback for setupmem.dmp, setupapi.dev.log, and event logs.
For down-level WSUS/WU failures (e.g. 0xC1900107), check BlueBox.log in Windows\Logs\Mosetup.

Know the setupact.log phase tags: CONX/MOUPG (down-level UI/compatibility, MOUPG = Store upgrade), PANTHR (mostly ignorable), Setup Platform (the core non-UI upgrade engine), IBSLIB (Image Based Setup Library), MIG (the migration engine moving data between OS images), and DISM (driver/service migration).

For a suspected device-install hang, search for 'ndv: Waiting for previous device install to complete' with an unclosed '<ins>' tag — each device install has a 5-minute timeout, and once one device hangs kernel PnP, every subsequent device install will also appear to hang.

When a rollback extended error code is unclear, decode it against the documented Upgrade Error Codes reference table — e.g. MOSETUP_E_INSTALLDISKSPACE_BLOCK (0xC190020E) means insufficient disk space was the real blocker, and ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (0x80070005) points to a permissions/lockdown conflict rather than a compatibility issue.

Search every log file under the Panther/rollback folders for the literal string ', error' to quickly shortlist which specific log actually contains the failure, then open just that one in TextAnalysisTool.NET or Notepad++ with keyword filtering (Ctrl+N to set a filter, Ctrl+H to show only filtered lines) rather than reading every log in full.

l1: Free up disk space and retry the upgrade.
Temporarily uninstall known incompatible third-party software, especially antivirus.
Disconnect non-essential USB peripherals before retrying.
Suspend BitLocker with 'manage-bde -protectors -disable C:' before upgrading.
Run Disk Cleanup or Storage Sense to reclaim space if the compatibility scan reports insufficient disk space.
Temporarily disable or uninstall third-party antivirus/security software known to interfere with in-place upgrades, then retry.
l2: 0xC1900101-0x20004/0x2000c/0x20017 (SafeOS phase): update drivers and BIOS, remove unused SATA/legacy devices, and ensure 'Download and install updates (recommended)' is accepted at upgrade start.
0xC1900101-0x30018/0x3000D (First boot phase): disconnect all peripherals except mouse/keyboard/display and update or roll back the flagged display or device driver.

0xC1900101-0x40017 with Citrix VDA installed: uninstall Citrix VDA, run the upgrade, then reinstall — or disable the CtxMcsWbc filter driver (set its Start value to 4 in the registry) as a workaround.
0x8007001F-0x3000D (First boot apply failure): check whether user profile folders were redirected to a non-OS drive; if so, correct the Profile Directory registry value back to the system drive.

For a kernel PnP device-install hang (often surfacing as ERROR_CANCELLED 0x800704C7), don't assume the first hung entry in the log is the true root cause — drvinst.exe processes acquire the mutex in a non-deterministic order, so compare timestamps; the recommended action is to remove or update the suspected driver after a rollback and retry the upgrade.

l1: Record the exact rollback or error code shown after failure, including the sub-code after the dash.
Note the source build, target build, and deployment method used.
Capture a screenshot of the failure screen if one is shown.
Confirm whether the device rolled back automatically to the previous build.
l2: Collect the full $WINDOWS.~BT\Sources\Panther folder (setupact.log, setuperr.log, miglog.xml).
Run SetupDiag.exe and attach the generated SetupDiagResults.xml/json (from %windir%\logs\SetupDiag starting 2004).
Collect supplemental rollback logs from $Windows.~BT\Sources\Rollback: setupmem.dmp, setupapi.dev.log, and event logs (*.evtx).
In Event Viewer, search Windows Logs > Application for 'winsetupdiag02' events for a structured failure summary.
For automated log capture, use the Windows Setup Diagnostics tool (SDCON) if available in the environment, or 'copylogs.cmd' as a fallback to gather the full upgrade log set.

Understand the difference between what SetupDiag, Logs.zip, and an SDP/copylogs.cmd collection each provide: SetupDiag attempts automatic root-cause analysis, Logs.zip is the minimal raw log set, and SDP/copylogs are broader collectors — none of them retrieve everything, so cross-check what's actually needed against what each one grabbed.

upgrade_rollback_failure.title: Upgrade fails and rolls back automatically (generic 0xC1900101)

steps.action: Confirm the device is back on the original build via winver
steps.expect: Rollback confirmed, device stable on prior build

steps.action: Run SetupDiag.exe against the Panther and Rollback logs
steps.expect: Returns a specific matching rollback profile and reason code

steps.action: Remediate the flagged driver, app, or disk space issue from SetupDiag's output
steps.expect: Blocking condition is resolved

steps.action: Retry the upgrade attempt
steps.expect: Upgrade completes and device boots to the target build

citrix_vda_blocks_upgrade_0x40017.title: Upgrade rolls back with 0xC1900101-0x40017 on a Citrix VDA machine

steps.action: Confirm the machine has Citrix Virtual Delivery Agent installed
steps.expect: Citrix VDA is present, typically with the CtxMcsWbc filter driver

steps.action: Check whether Cumulative Update for the current Windows version already includes the documented fix
steps.expect: Confirms whether a simple update resolves it or a workaround is needed

steps.action: Uninstall Citrix VDA using VDAWorkstationSetup, run the upgrade, then reinstall VDA afterward
steps.expect: Upgrade completes without the filter driver blocking disk writes

steps.action: Alternative: set CtxMcsWbc's Start registry value from 0 to 4 to disable the MCS cache service, then delete the CtxMcsWbc key and restart
steps.expect: Filter driver no longer blocks the upgrade

steps.action: Retry the Windows upgrade
steps.expect: Upgrade completes without rollback

profile_redirect_rollback_0x8007001f.title: First boot apply fails (0x8007001F-0x3000D) due to redirected user profiles

steps.action: Check SetupDiag output for 'FindRollbackFailure' with Last Operation = First boot apply
steps.expect: Confirms error 0x8007001F-0x3000D at the First Boot phase

steps.action: Check whether user profiles were moved to a non-OS drive (e.g. E:) via the ProfilesDirectory registry value
steps.expect: Confirms the profile directory points off the system drive

steps.action: Correct HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList\ProfilesDirectory back to the system drive
steps.expect: Registry value now points to the OS drive

steps.action: Retry the upgrade
steps.expect: First boot phase completes without the 0x8007001F rollback

kernel_pnp_device_install_hang_0x800704c.title: Upgrade hangs/cancels with ERROR_CANCELLED (0x800704C7) during device install

steps.action: Search setupact.log for 'ndv: Waiting for previous device install to complete' with an unclosed '<ins>' tag
steps.expect: Confirms a specific device install never completed within its 5-minute window

steps.action: Compare timestamps across all hung/unclosed device install sections rather than trusting log order (drvinst.exe mutex order is non-deterministic)
steps.expect: Identifies the earliest genuine hang, which is the most likely true root cause

steps.action: After the automatic rollback, remove or update the suspected driver identified from the earliest hang
steps.expect: Driver is updated or removed cleanly

steps.action: Retry the upgrade
steps.expect: Device install phase completes without exceeding the timeout

steps.action: If it fails again, repeat isolation on the new log and consider reproducing under a kernel debugger if no new suspect driver is found
steps.expect: A definitive faulting driver is identified and remediated

insufficient_disk_space_block.title: Upgrade won't start — compatibility scan reports insufficient disk space

steps.action: Check the exact free space reported versus the minimum required (typically 20–32GB depending on version)
steps.expect: Confirms the shortfall and how much space needs to be freed

steps.action: Run Storage Sense or 'cleanmgr /sageset:1' to identify what's consuming space (old Windows.old, temp files, hibernation file)
steps.expect: Identifies safe-to-remove space consumers

steps.action: Clear the identified space, or attach external/USB storage if the upgrade tool supports it for temporary staging
steps.expect: Free space now exceeds the minimum requirement

steps.action: Re-run the compatibility scan or restart the upgrade
steps.expect: Disk space check passes and the upgrade proceeds

antivirus_blocks_upgrade_process.title: Third-party antivirus blocks or repeatedly fails the upgrade

steps.action: Check SetupDiag output or setupact.log for a reference to the AV product or its filter driver around the failure point
steps.expect: Confirms the AV software's involvement rather than an unrelated cause

steps.action: Confirm whether the AV vendor has a documented Windows-upgrade-compatible version or an uninstall/reinstall requirement
steps.expect: Identifies the correct remediation path for that specific product

steps.action: Uninstall the AV product (not just disable it, since drivers often remain loaded), run the upgrade, then reinstall a supported version afterward
steps.expect: Upgrade completes without the AV filter driver interfering

steps.action: Confirm the device is on the target build and reinstall/verify the AV product afterward
steps.expect: Device is upgraded and protected again
